prepared_main_difference: origin/main was a207786205bff0919eb2c8c9126c67f302ccff34 at review time; review comparisons used the required recorded base
summary: The candidate is a partial fix. It corrects the issue's two explicit two-increment reproductions and split-marker handling, but still drops trailing text when a complete tool call and its suffix arrive in the final increment. FunctionCallParser.parse_stream_end() cannot recover the suffix because MiMoDetector inherits the no-op BaseFormatDetector.finish().

tests.what_was_measured: Direct reproduction showed trailing text retained forever, split marker markup leaked, and one-character chunking failed to detect the call. Assertions were evaluated from emitted results and detector buffer state.
Candidate regression: 4 tests and all 10 marker-split subtests passed.
Independent chunk-boundary matrix. Reported examples and one-character chunks passed, but final call-plus-text retained the text, and two calls in the final chunk emitted only the first.
Actual public serving parser path: parse_stream_chunk emitted the call while buffering 'After.'; parse_stream_end returned no text/calls and left the buffer unchanged.

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and remaining counterexamples are deterministic CPU-only string parser behavior. No GPU claim was needed or made.

remaining_counterexamples: A final stream increment equal to COMPLETE_TOOL_CALL + 'After.' emits the call but never emits 'After.', including after FunctionCallParser.parse_stream_end().
A final stream increment containing COMPLETE_TOOL_CALL + inter-call text + COMPLETE_TOOL_CALL + trailing text emits only the first call and strands the remainder.
MiMo detect_and_parse itself omits normal text after tool-call blocks, so the issue's stated one-shot/streaming accumulated-text equivalence remains unmet.
remaining_limitations: No MiMo model weights or HTTP server were used; model semantics and tokenizer chunk production were not validated.
No GPU execution was performed because the reviewed implementation is pure Python parsing.
No native code changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
The review used one prepared x86_64/ROCm environment and makes no multi-node or alternate-architecture claim.
